# Colten Ellis

**Colten Ellis** (born October 5, 2000) is a Canadian professional ice hockey player who serves as a goaltender for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League (NHL). Originally drafted by the St. Louis Blues in the third round (93rd overall) of the 2019 NHL Entry Draft, Ellis began his professional career with the Blues' minor league affiliates before being claimed by the Buffalo Sabres on waivers in October 2025. He made his NHL debut that month, establishing himself as one of the team's goaltenders.

Ellis earned recognition as one of Atlantic Canada's most promising young goaltenders while competing in regional hockey and major junior competitions. During his junior career, he posted some of the best statistical performances in recent Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL) history, including numerous single-season records and awards.

# Early Life and Youth Hockey

Ellis was born in River Denys, Nova Scotia, and grew up in the Cape Breton region. He began his hockey career with local youth programs before progressing to competitive levels. Playing for the Cape Breton West Islanders, a major midget team, Ellis gained provincial recognition and led his team to the Telus Cup national championship in 2017. The victory marked the first time an Atlantic Canada team had won the national midget title. During the tournament, Ellis was named player of the game in an opening match, stopping 34 shots in a 2-1 victory.

# Junior Hockey Career

### Cape Breton Screaming Eagles

Ellis was drafted by the Cape Breton Screaming Eagles in the fourth round (59th overall) of the 2016 QMJHL Entry Draft. He appeared in three games for the Eagles during the 2016-17 season before being traded to the Rimouski Océanic.

### Rimouski Océanic

After his trade to Rimouski, Ellis established himself as a starting goaltender for the Océanic. During the 2017-18 season, his first full year with the team, Ellis posted a 33-8-1 record with 2.35 goals-against average, a .913 save percentage, and six shutouts in 51 games. The following season, he recorded 27 wins and three shutouts across 46 games. In his final season with Rimouski (2019-20), Ellis compiled 18 wins and two shutouts in 29 games while maintaining a 2.41 goals-against average and .904 save percentage.

### Charlottetown Islanders

Ellis completed his junior career with the Charlottetown Islanders during the 2020-21 season, which took place under COVID-19 restrictions. In a remarkably successful season, Ellis compiled a 23-1-0 record across 24 games, posting a 1.78 goals-against average, a .926 save percentage, and seven shutouts. His performance led the QMJHL in wins and established a new career QMJHL shutout record. Ellis also earned the award for best goaltender of the year and received a spot on the first all-star team. Following this exceptional final junior season, he signed a three-year entry-level contract with the St. Louis Blues.

# Professional Career

### St. Louis Blues Organization

Ellis signed with the St. Louis Blues in February 2021 and began his professional career in their minor league system. During the 2021-22 season, his rookie year, Ellis split time between the Worcester Railers of the ECHL and the Springfield Thunderbirds of the American Hockey League (AHL). With Worcester, he appeared in 34 games with a 15-13-5 record, 3.21 goals-against average, and .905 save percentage. He earned six combined AHL appearances with Springfield.

The 2022-23 season proved challenging for Ellis. With limited opportunities in Springfield due to competition from other prospects, he was assigned to the ECHL's Tulsa Oilers, where he appeared in 27 games. Midway through the season, Ellis underwent hip surgery in early 2023, which ended his season early. During his rehabilitation at his home in Nova Scotia, Ellis underwent a significant perspective shift regarding his career. He later credited this time away from hockey with helping him rediscover his passion for the sport and improving his mental approach to competition.

Ellis returned to action with the Orlando Solar Bears of the ECHL during the 2023-24 season, appearing in 21 games with improved statistics including a 2.45 goals-against average and .923 save percentage. He was subsequently called up to Springfield in January 2024 and did not return to the ECHL. During the 2024-25 season, Ellis established himself as a primary goaltender for Springfield, recording a 22-14-3 record, a 2.63 goals-against average, a .922 save percentage, and three shutouts across 42 games.

### Buffalo Sabres

In October 2025, the St. Louis Blues placed Ellis on waivers, and the Buffalo Sabres claimed him. Ellis made his NHL debut on October 22, 2025, against the Detroit Red Wings, earning a 4-2 victory and stopping 31 of 33 shots for a .939 save percentage. With this appearance, Ellis became the 770th player in ECHL history to reach the NHL and the first Cape Breton-born goaltender to earn a victory in the league.

Following his debut, Ellis saw increased playing time with the Sabres. By mid-November 2025, he had compiled a 3-1-0 record across early appearances, including a notable performance against the Edmonton Oilers on November 17, where he recorded a .970 save percentage in a 5-1 victory. As of December 2025, Ellis had appeared in multiple games for Buffalo and was competing for time in the team's goaltending rotation alongside other netminders.

# Playing Style

Ellis is described as an athletic goaltender with strong positioning and quick reflexes. He demonstrates good mechanical form and maintains composure during games. His development as a goaltender has emphasized consistency and mental resilience, particularly following his return from hip surgery.

# Career Statistics

Ellis holds a career QMJHL shutout record and previously set the best goals-against average single-season record in the league. His 2020-21 season with Charlottetown ranks among the most successful single seasons by a goaltender in recent QMJHL history.

## Personal Life

Ellis is from River Denys, Nova Scotia. He has a brother named Matthew Ellis and a cousin named Chase Ellis, also in hockey.

Sports
------

Cape Breton West Islanders open Telus Cup with 2-1 win over Quebec
------------------------------------------------------------------

![Image 1](https://www.invernessoran.ca/images/slideshow_2017_01/Apr26-17Sports.jpg)

_Colten Ellis was player of the game on Monday, stopping 34 Quebec shots to lead the Cape Breton West Islanders to a 2-1 win in their opening game of the Telus Cup. He’s shown here receiving his Atlantic Major Midget gold medal in Miramichi earlier this month._

* * *

\-by Bill Dunphy

There’s a saying that goes: ‘You can’t win ‘em all.’ And there’s a corollary to that which goes: ‘You can’t win ‘em all if you don’t win the first one.’  
    Nobody expects anyone in a six-team hockey tournament to win every game, but when you’re deemed to be the underdog, winning game one is a good start.  
    The Cape Breton West Islanders did just that in their first game of the Telus Cup Major Midget national tournament on Monday, defeating the Blizzard du Séminaire Saint-François 2-1.

Colten Ellis was stellar in goal for the Islanders, making 34 saves, including 12 in the second period when Cape Breton West was tagged with three minor penalties in a span of nine minutes.  
    Two members of the Braveheart line provided Cape Breton West’s goals.  
    Malcolm MacEachern put the Islanders up 1-0 at 4:36 of the first period, taking a pass in the slot from defenceman Liam MacKinnon to wire it past the Quebec goalie. The Islanders were up 6-1 on shots at that point.  
    Quebec answered with a shorthanded goal before the period was out.  
    Cape Breton West started the second period with a powerplay and fellow Braveheart Jacob Stewart took advantage, scoring the eventual winning goal at 1:16 on a play with Logan Timmons and Ryan MacLellan.  
    From then on it was a goaltender’s duel, with Ellis coming out on top. Quebec also had a powerplay with 4:29 left in the third and pulled their goalie with two minutes left, but Ellis stopped all 11 shots he faced in the final frame.  
    It was the first time in 12 years that the Atlantic Region champion has beaten the Quebec Region champion in the preliminary round; Cole Harbour edged Lévis 4-3 at the 2005 tournament.  
    In a telephone interview after the game, Islanders coach Kyle MacDonald said the win goes a long way in building confidence.  
    “It was the start we were looking for,” said MacDonald. “We’re considered the underdogs, but within our room there’s a belief, and not a false belief, that we’re a contender to win this tournament.”  
    With his win in goal, Ellis was named player of the game.  
    “I’m not surprised by that,” MacDonald said. “It was exciting to see him play so well at a national championship. It was our biggest game of the year and he was outstanding. Colten gives us the belief that we can win in any situation.”  
    As for the Bravehearts making such a huge contribution to the win, MacDonald said it’s what they’ve come to expect.  
    “Guys who work as hard as they do find success, especially in the playoffs. You see it all the time in the NHL. They provide great leadership and make the next line that follows them work just as hard.”  
    The Islanders were up against the Pacific Region champs, the Leduc (Alta.) Oil Kings, yesterday (Tuesday). A win in this game would mark the first time an Atlantic team won back-to-back games since the Antigonish Novas did it in 1981.  
    Today (Wednesday) they play the host Prince George Caribou; on Thursday they face the Central Region champs, the Mississauga Rebels (game will be shown live on the big screen at Strathspey Place at 8 p.m.); and they wrap up the round-robin on Friday with a game against the West Region champs, the Regina Pat Canadians.  
    The semifinals are on Saturday and the Sunday’s final will be broadcast live on TSN.
